title: Workdir, Context & Ignoring Files 🎯
description: Set working directories, understand build context, and use .dockerignore to speed up builds.

slides.title: `WORKDIR` – Your Home Inside the Image 🏠
slides.content:
# Set the Default Directory

```dockerfile
WORKDIR /path/to/dir
```

- Creates the directory if it doesn't exist.
- All subsequent `RUN`, `CMD`, `ENTRYPOINT`, `COPY`, `ADD` commands will execute from this path.
- You can have multiple `WORKDIR` instructions; they are relative to the previous one if not absolute.

**Example:**
```dockerfile
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .   # copies to /app
```

> Best practice: Use `WORKDIR` instead of `RUN cd /some/dir`. `cd` does not persist across layers.

quizData.question: Why is `WORKDIR /app` preferred over `RUN cd /app` in a Dockerfile?

options.text: `cd` only affects the current RUN layer; `WORKDIR` persists for subsequent instructions

quizData.explanation: Each RUN runs in a new shell, so a `cd` has no effect on later instructions. WORKDIR sets the directory for the entire image build.

slides.title: The Build Context Deep Dive 📦
slides.content:
# What Gets Sent to the Daemon?

When you run `docker build .`, Docker packages the entire directory (recursively) and sends it to the daemon. This includes:

- All files and subdirectories
- Hidden files (`.` files, `.git`)
- `node_modules`, build artifacts, etc.

This can be HUGE and slow down the build.

**Solution: `.dockerignore`** file – similar to `.gitignore` – lists files/folders to exclude from the context.

Example `.dockerignore`:
```
node_modules
.git
*.md
Dockerfile
.dockerignore
```

slides.title: Using .dockerignore 🧹
slides.content: Create a `.dockerignore` in the same directory as your Dockerfile:

quizData.question: What is the primary purpose of `.dockerignore`?

options.text: To exclude sensitive files from the final image
To reduce the size of the build context sent to the daemon
To tell Docker which files to ignore when running containers

quizData.explanation: `.dockerignore` prevents files from being sent in the build context, speeding up builds and avoiding accidental inclusion.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always Create a .dockerignore
Even if you have a tiny project, a `.dockerignore` prevents the `Dockerfile` itself and Git history from bloating the context. Minimize context size for faster builds.
